findings.F1: The book's losses come from its short side. It was short on 51 % of bars, with a mean gain of -0.094 % per bar (t -4.75), against +0.032 % per bar on its 45 % of long bars (t 1.86). The coin's next-day return was +0.171 % after short bars and +0.087 % after long bars, so the forecast was short just before the larger rises.
findings.F2: The book moved against the coins. Its daily returns correlate -0.20 with the coins' daily returns over 2898 days, and its mean is -0.037 % a day against +0.117 % for holding. On its worst 2 % of days the book lost 6.2 % while the coin rose 4.1 % that same day.
findings.F3: No signal predicts the next 5 days clearly. Among the components' standardised values, nearness to the 90-day high correlates -0.038 with the 5-day excess return (t -2.2, 3254 cases), low volatility -0.042 (t -2.4), and the forecast -0.035 (t -1.99). Momentum (-0.0002) and reversal (0.001) show nothing. Every quintile table is non-monotonic (high: +0.79 %, +0.11 %, +0.14 %, -0.87 %, -0.17 %), and about ten such measures were looked at, so none stands out from chance.
findings.F4: Saturdays stand out. Averaged across coins, Saturday's excess daily return is +0.33 % (t 2.2, 414 days), and Saturday minus the other days is positive in 19 of 24 windows (t 2.34). It is also positive in all 6 coins (t 0.35 to 2.58). But this is the best of 7 weekdays tested, and a weekday is an on/off condition with no grading.
findings.F5: Volatility tells you how big the next move is, not which way. The absolute 5-day move rises steadily with the 10-day volatility quintile, from 5.5 % in the lowest to 9.0 % in the highest. The mean 5-day return does not rise with it (0.39 %, 0.76 %, 0.99 %, 0.85 %, 0.54 %).
findings.F6: Past returns do not grade the next 5 days. Last-day-return quintiles are non-monotonic (second quintile -1.58 %, t -3.7; fourth +1.05 %, t 2.1; correlation 0.014, 3117 cases). The 20-day return correlates 0.036 overall (t 1.87), but ranges from -0.05 to +0.13 by coin.

no_ideas: The only pattern that is consistent across windows and coins is the Saturday excess return (F4). It is the best of seven weekdays tested and an on/off condition with no grading. Every graded angle tested (the components, the forecast, past returns, the volatility level) was non-monotonic or too weak to tell apart from chance (F3, F5, F6), so no finding supports a graded idea.
